guards.what: G2 (DORMANT): C# gates on `props.IsPoweredAttack()`; the sim's modify_hp_lost signature carries no props at all, so the port substitutes `card is None or card.is_unpowered`
guards.issue: MECHANISM: ValuePropExtensions.IsPoweredAttack (ValuePropExtensions.cs:5-12) is `props.HasFlag(Move) && !props.HasFlag(Unpowered)` -- a property of the DAMAGE CALL. the_boot.py:37 asks about the CARD instead: `if card is None or card.is_unpowered: return amount`, where Card.is_unpowered is a class attribute set on curses and statuses (cards/base.py:64). The two disagree in both directions. (a) A card that deals non-Move or explicitly Unpowered damage while not itself being an is_unpowered card: the sim raises it, C# does not. (b) Card-less powered-Move damage dealt by the player: C# raises it, the sim bails. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, both directions, executed -- `py audit/tools/relic_probes_b16.py boot-props`). For (b) the probe finds NO ported site: every DamageCmd.deal in powers.py and relics/ that omits `card=` passes DamageProps.NON_CARD_UNPOWERED or NON_CARD_HP_LOSS, and monster moves are the player's dealer-check away. For (a) there is exactly ONE ported site that aims at an enemy -- Omnislice's splash leg (cards/colorless_attacks.py:320-325, `props=DamageProps.CARD_UNPOWERED, card=self`, and Omnislice is a normal Attack so is_unpowered is False); the other nine sites (bad_luck, beckon, blood_wall, bloodletting, brand, hemokinesis, offering, regret, enchantments.py:500) all target the PLAYER and are stopped by the `target is self.player` bail. And Omnislice still cannot produce a difference: its splash amount is the FIRST leg's returned `dealt`, and the first leg is DamageProps.CARD -- a powered Move -- which The Boot has already floored at 5, so the splash can never arrive inside the 1..4 window while the relic is held. Executed confirmation of that: with `_damage` forced to 3 the sim reports HP lost [5, 5] and so does the C# trace. What would make it live: porting a card that deals unpowered or unblockable damage to an ENEMY with an amount that is not derived from a powered leg -- or fixing the sim's modify_hp_lost to carry props, which is the correct fix and would close this without a content change. Rule 7: cards/colorless_attacks.py, cards/base.py, powers.py and valueprops.py are not hashed here.

guards.rationale: The relic's text reads '4 or less -> 5', so the two vars are the same number expressed twice and the source only wires up one of them. the_boot.py:25 pins MINIMUM = 5 and the port's `if 1 <= amount < self.MINIMUM: return self.MINIMUM` reproduces C#'s three-branch form exactly (`amount < 1` -> unchanged, `amount >= 5` -> unchanged, else 5). No AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 5 and 4 are the pinned non-ascension values. PROMPT.md bug class 19 says to re-read every numeric against the C# even when the port names the C# expression; done, and both agree.

guards.what: N3: the `amount < 1` bail (TheBoot.cs:40-43) vs the sim's `1 <= amount` plus DamageCmd's own `if hp_lost > 0` gate (cmds.py:83-87)
guards.rationale: C# calls Hook.ModifyHpLost unconditionally, including with a zero amount after a full block, and The Boot returns it unchanged; the sim never calls the hook at 0 at all. Same outcome (a fully blocked hit costs 0 HP either way), and the relic's own `1 <=` clause makes the port correct even where the sim's caller does dispatch. Recorded because a floor-to-5 relic is exactly the shape where a missing zero guard would turn a blocked hit into 5 damage.

guards.what: N4: `target == base.Owner.Creature -> return amount` (TheBoot.cs:32-35) vs `target is self.player` (the_boot.py:34)
guards.rationale: Both are identity comparisons against the owning player's creature (Relic.player returns CombatState.player, relics/base.py:282-284, which is the sim's player Creature). Not a side comparison on either side, so a player-side minion -- if the sim ever gets one -- would be treated the same way by both, unlike the side-vs-identity split recorded at relic/unsettling_lamp G3.
